name: History
dimension: what the sentence asserts about the human past

objects.label: Occurrence
objects.text: HI.O.A1 Occurrence

objects.label: The event
objects.text: HI.O.A1.1 The event — the unit of record, separated from its interpretation (the fact–interpretation distinction, E. H. Carr, *What Is History?*, 1961).

objects.label: The actor
objects.text: HI.O.A1.2 The actor — persons and groups; prosopography (collective biography).

objects.label: The place
objects.text: HI.O.A1.3 The place — located with EA tools; the claim of human presence is HI.

objects.label: Authenticity of the record
objects.text: HI.O.A1.4 Authenticity of the record — forgery and interpolation. Lorenzo Valla showed the Donation of Constantine to be a forgery (c. 1440) by philology.

objects.label: Time
objects.text: HI.O.A2 Time

objects.label: Absolute date
objects.text: HI.O.A2.1 Absolute date — calendars and eras: Julian, Gregorian (introduced 1582), AH, BCE/CE.

objects.label: Relative order
objects.text: HI.O.A2.2 Relative order — terminus post quem and ante quem.

objects.label: Synchronism
objects.text: HI.O.A2.3 Synchronism — aligning independent records of the same moment.

objects.label: Periodisation
objects.text: HI.O.A2.4 Periodisation — labels such as "the Renaissance" are conventions (W12), not discoveries.

objects.label: Scientific dating
objects.text: HI.O.A2.5 Scientific dating — radiocarbon and dendrochronology dates are measurements owned by EA and PH; HI uses them.

objects.label: Cause
objects.text: HI.O.A3 Cause

objects.label: Reasons of actors
objects.text: HI.O.A3.1 Reasons of actors — Collingwood's re-enactment of thought (*The Idea of History*, 1946).

objects.label: Conditions and structures
objects.text: HI.O.A3.2 Conditions and structures — necessary and sufficient conditions; structural causes.

objects.label: Contingency
objects.text: HI.O.A3.3 Contingency and chance.

objects.label: Counterfactuals
objects.text: HI.O.A3.4 Counterfactual claims — they owe W7 for their premises and W9 for the inference. Unconstrained counterfactuals are a heuristic.

objects.label: Model-explained paths
objects.text: HI.O.A3.5 Model-explained paths — when a growth path is explained by an economic model, the explanation is EC and HI supplies the record (cliometrics is a bridge).

objects.label: Change and continuity
objects.text: HI.O.A4 Change and continuity

objects.label: Durations
objects.text: HI.O.A4.1 Durations — Braudel's three: longue durée, conjoncture and événement (*La Méditerranée*, 1949).

objects.label: Processes
objects.text: HI.O.A4.2 Processes — industrialisation, state formation. A demographic transition is cited from MS.

objects.label: Structures over time
objects.text: HI.O.A4.3 Structures over time — institutions, economies, environments in human time.

objects.label: Comparison across places
objects.text: HI.O.A4.4 Comparison across places — comparative history; world and global history.

objects.label: Meaning and memory
objects.text: HI.O.A5 Meaning and memory

objects.label: Meaning to participants
objects.text: HI.O.A5.1 Meaning to participants — the history of mentalités.

objects.label: Collective memory
objects.text: HI.O.A5.2 Collective memory — Halbwachs (1925); lieux de mémoire (Nora, 1984–92).

objects.label: Heritage and commemoration
objects.text: HI.O.A5.3 Heritage and commemoration — monuments, museums. A heritage-law duty is LA.

objects.label: Historiography
objects.text: HI.O.A5.4 Historiography — what later historians made of the past. Schools of interpretation are answer-families, not cells.

objects.label: Oral history
objects.text: HI.O.A5.5 Oral history — a dated account owes W7 like any record. A tradition-internal account (whakapapa as authority) is IK under W13 and does not travel into A1 without W7.

warrants.defeaters: two independent authenticated sources, or one with no plausible rival

warrants.standard: W4 (dating, owned by EA or PH)

warrants.defeaters: mechanism shown in the record; rival causes considered
series built from records; method stated

bridges_table: science (MSC 01 bridge; the theorem is MA)

sections.governing_thought:
History is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five assertions about the past: occurrence, time, cause, change and continuity, and meaning and memory.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **what the sentence asserts about the human past.** Order: from the single fact to its meaning.
1. Occurrence
2. Time
3. Cause
4. Change and continuity
5. Meaning and memory

A period, region or nation is a catalogue (substrate), not a cell. "Medieval Europe" indexes claims; it does not hold them.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. The dated fact is history's. That an event occurred, and when, is HI; every other pyramid cites it.
2. The model-explained path is the model's (EC, PO, ST); HI supplies the record.
3. A mathematician's life is HI; the theorem is MA; MSC 01 is the bridge.
4. A physical date (radiocarbon) is a measurement in EA or PH; its use for a human event is HI.
5. A strategic lesson drawn from a case is ST; the case's facts are HI.
6. A tradition-internal account of the past is IK or RE under W13; it enters HI.O.A1 only by W7.
7. A legal rule in force at a date is LA; the history of that rule is HI.
sections.scope_boundary:

|---|---|
| the theorem, law or mechanism itself | MA, PH, BI and others |
| the strategic lesson | ST |
| economic explanation by model | EC |
| tradition-internal authority over the past | IK, RE (W13) |
